items.title: Jim Cullum interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007
items.q: ‘cause Eddie Condon writes in this book

ctx.x: Okay here’s a little scenario. The time machine is a reality. Could you pick a couple of times that you’d like to go back to and be around when something happened in jazz history?

Well let me tell you. Everybody that plays this game, right, everybody that’s a jazz lover and a jazz fan, has these little — plays this little game in their head. And you go back and you think, and ‘cause Eddie Condon writes in this book and it says and so and he says so © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -16-

he meets Bix and Bix says he wants to go down to hear King Oliver. So they all go to hear King Oliver and they go down there and they stand there and Eddie Condon hadn’t been there himself. And he says and so one of the guys says the big guy, that’s Oliver, and that other guy’s just come from New Orleans, that’s the little guy, and his name is Armstrong and his name is Armstrong.
